title: Frontend: typed API client generated from backend/openapi.json
description: Generates src/api/types.ts from the committed backend/openapi.json snapshot and builds the thin typed client + MSW mocks every feature task depends on. No UI in this task — this is the data layer only.

checklist.step: Add openapi-typescript as a dev dependency and a script to generate src/api/types.ts from ../backend/openapi.json — never hand-edit types.ts.

Build src/api/client.ts: a thin fetch wrapper (base URL config, JSON parsing) that maps every documented error case (404/422/503, per API.md's 'Error Cases to Cover in Tests') to a typed ApiError with status and detail.
Build src/api/stocks.ts: getStockAnalysis(ticker) and getStockHistory(ticker, { range, interval }) typed against the generated types.
Build src/api/portfolio.ts: getPortfolio(), getPortfolioRisk(), addPosition(payload), deletePosition(id) typed against the generated types.

Build tests/mocks/handlers.ts (MSW) mirroring every endpoint in API.md, including the merge-on-duplicate-ticker POST behavior and every error case in API.md's error-cases section — this becomes the shared mock layer every later feature task's tests reuse.
Unit-test api/client.ts's error-mapping logic directly (each status code maps to the right ApiError shape) — this module needs its own tests since no feature UI exists yet to exercise it indirectly.

decisions.decision: Installed openapi-typescript@^7.13.0 with npm's --legacy-peer-deps, since its published peerDependencies range (typescript ^5.x) predates this project's pinned typescript ~6.0.2 and npm's default resolver refuses the install otherwise.
decisions.rationale: openapi-typescript is a devDependency / build-time code generator only — it never ships in the runtime bundle — and its generated output (src/api/types.ts) type-checked cleanly under typescript 6.0.3 with no errors, so the peer-range mismatch is a stale peerDependencies declaration on the package's side, not a real incompatibility. Rejected alternative: downgrading the project's typescript version to satisfy the peer range, which would undo a decision already made in frontend-scaffold for no functional benefit.

decisions.decision: api/client.ts resolves its base URL from import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL, defaulting to '' (same-origin) when unset; every endpoint path passed to request() already includes the '/api' prefix per API.md.
decisions.rationale: Neither API.md nor Frontend.md pins down how the frontend locates the backend at runtime (dev-server proxy vs. same-origin production deploy vs. a separate host). An env var with an empty-string default keeps local dev and a same-origin production deploy working with zero configuration, while still giving a future task (or ops config) a single seam to point at a different host. Rejected alternative: hardcoding a localhost:8000 default, which would silently misbehave in any non-local deployment instead of failing loudly.

decisions.decision: tests/mocks/handlers.ts reaches every documented error case through sentinel tickers/ids/payload values (e.g. GET /api/stocks/UNKNOWN/analysis -> 404, ticker 'NOPROVIDER' -> 503, ticker 'THINHISTORY' -> 422 insufficient history, POST payload ticker 'OVERFLOW' -> 422 merge-overflow ErrorDetail) baked into the default handler list, rather than a parallel set of per-scenario handlers every consuming test must opt into via server.use().
decisions.rationale: Keeps the shared mock layer's surface area small and self-documenting for the many feature tasks that will import these handlers — a component test can hit an error path by requesting a sentinel ticker/id with the exact same handler registration as the happy path, with no need to learn MSW's server.use() override API just to exercise an error state. Rejected alternative: exporting a second `errorHandlers` map for tests to layer in, which duplicates each endpoint's routing logic and adds an extra import every error-path test needs.

decisions.decision: The mock POST /api/portfolio/positions handler stores only the always-known PositionOut fields (id, ticker, quantity, avg_cost_basis, entry_date) and computes current_price/unrealized_pnl_pct at GET-time from a small mockPrices lookup, rather than storing/mutating those two fields directly on the position.
decisions.rationale: API.md is explicit that current_price/unrealized_pnl_pct are always null in the POST response itself but are enriched on a later read — storing them directly on the position object made the POST-response-is-always-null rule and the GET-is-enriched rule fight over the same field, so the mock's initial implementation left a freshly-merged position permanently null-priced even after a subsequent GET, which is a smaller-but-still-real deviation from the documented contract this task's mock layer exists to encode correctly for every later feature test. Rejected alternative: leaving current_price null forever after any merge, which was simpler but wrong per API.md.

comments.summary: `npm run format:check` (Prettier, configured in package.json/.prettierrc.json) fails on this branch: the new `npm run generate:api-types` row added to frontend/README.md's script table isn't padded to the table's column widths, which is what Prettier's markdown formatter enforces. Confirmed this is introduced by this PR (main's README.md passes format:check cleanly; checking out this PR's README.md reproduces the failure) and not pre-existing. Fix with `npm run format` (or manually pad the row) and recommit.

Non-blocking: the mock POST /api/portfolio/positions handler's OVERFLOW-sentinel check compares `body.ticker.toUpperCase()` without trimming, unlike the merge path two lines later which uses `body.ticker.trim().toUpperCase()` (and unlike PositionIn's own documented whitespace-stripping normalization in types.ts). A whitespace-padded ' OVERFLOW ' ticker silently skips the intended 422 merge-overflow response and creates a real position instead. Tracked as a follow-up.

Non-blocking: the mock's per-field validation-error branch only ever reports one invalid field (quantity XOR avg_cost_basis) even when both are simultaneously invalid, unlike real FastAPI/pydantic which lists every failing field in one HTTPValidationError. A test relying on this mock to exercise the multi-field case would pass against the mock while diverging from the real backend's actual response shape. Tracked as a follow-up.

Non-blocking, not introduced by this PR (vite.config.ts's coverage config predates it, from frontend-scaffold): `vitest run --coverage`'s text reporter prints an empty per-file table (no rows, no 'All files' summary row) even though the underlying v8/lcov data and the 90% threshold gate both work correctly (verified against coverage/lcov.info: every file's LF/LH match, aggregate 100%). This makes the CI-equivalent console output impossible to sanity-check by eye when investigating a future coverage regression. Noticed while running the required coverage check for this review; tracked as a follow-up since it would otherwise be forgotten once this PR's comments disappear on merge.

review.notes: Full review performed: checked out PR #63, ran backend pytest --cov (99.84%, 472 passed) and frontend vitest --coverage (52 passed, 100% stmts/branches/funcs/lines against the 90% gate), npm run lint (clean), npm run build (tsc -b + vite build, clean), npm run build-storybook (clean), and npm run format:check (fails — see blocking comment). Regenerated src/api/types.ts from backend/openapi.json myself and diffed byte-for-byte against the committed file: identical, confirming it is genuinely generated and never hand-edited. Verified client.ts's extractDetail correctly distinguishes and normalizes both documented 422 shapes (ErrorDetail vs HTTPValidationError) against backend/openapi.json's actual per-route responses (add_position and get_stock_history declare `anyOf` HTTPValidationError|ErrorDetail on 422; get_stock_analysis declares plain ErrorDetail on 422) and both are covered by client.test.ts. Verified handlers.ts's merge-on-duplicate-ticker logic against API.md and portfolio.test.ts's assertions: quantity summed (100+100=200), avg_cost_basis quantity-weighted ((100*195.30+100*205.30)/200=200.30), entry_date keeps the earlier date — all correct. Reproduced the --legacy-peer-deps decision's premise directly: `npm install` without the flag in a scratch copy of package.json/package-lock.json fails with an ERESOLVE conflict purely on openapi-typescript's `peer typescript@^5.x` vs the project's pinned `typescript ~6.0.2`; openapi-typescript is a dev-only code generator (never ships in the runtime bundle) and its generated output type-checks cleanly under `tsc -b`, confirming the workaround is justified rather than masking a real incompatibility. This task adds no components/pages (data layer only, per its own description), so step 7a's placement check and the browser walkthrough (step 9) don't apply — there is no UI surface to click through. Ran the code-review skill (medium effort) against the diff in addition to my own manual pass; it found the two mock-fidelity issues recorded above as non-blocking. The one blocking finding (README.md Prettier formatting) is trivial to fix but is a genuine, PR-introduced failure of a tool this project has configured and documented (`npm run format:check`), so per review process this is needs_work rather than accepted-with-a-nit.
